title: Filing Relief for Natural Disasters Act

claims.claim: Lets the IRS postpone federal tax deadlines after a state-declared disaster
claims.sourceSpan:
Authority To Postpone Federal Tax Deadlines by Reason of State-
Declared Disasters

claims.claim: (not just a federal one)
claims.sourceSpan:
may, upon the written request of the Governor of a State (or the
Mayor, in the case of the District of Columbia), apply the rules
of subsections (a) and (b) to a qualified State declared
disaster in the same manner as a disaster, fire, or action
otherwise described in subsection (a)
claims.note: Additive: the new subsection (c) applies the existing rules of (a)/(b) 'in the same manner as a disaster ... otherwise described in subsection (a)', i.e. alongside the pre-existing federal-declaration path.

claims.claim: Authorizes the IRS to postpone federal tax deadlines for state-declared disasters and lengthens the mandatory extension period.

Declared Disasters

claims.sourceSpan: inserting after subsection (b) the following new subsection
claims.note: Amends 'Section 7508A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986'; the inserted subsection is '``(c) ... Special Rule for State-Declared Disasters'.

claims.claim: (natural catastrophes, or any fire, flood, or explosion of sufficient severity)
claims.sourceSpan:
any
natural catastrophe (including any hurricane, tornado, storm,
high water, winddriven water, tidal wave, tsunami, earthquake,
volcanic eruption, landslide, mudslide, snowstorm, or drought),
or, regardless of cause, any fire, flood, or explosion, in any
part of the State, which in the determination of the Governor of
such State (or the Mayor, in the case of the District of
Columbia) causes damage of sufficient severity and magnitude
claims.note: 'of sufficient severity' faithfully compresses 'causes damage of sufficient severity and magnitude to warrant the application of the rules of this section'.

claims.claim: 'State' includes D.C., Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Northern Mariana Islands.

claims.claim: The changes apply to declarations made after enactment.
claims.sourceSpan:
The amendments
made by this section shall apply to declarations made after the date of
the enactment of this Act

claims.claim: The bill lets governors request federal tax postponements but does not require the IRS to grant a request.
claims.sourceSpan:
may, upon the written request of the Governor of a State (or the
Mayor, in the case of the District of Columbia), apply the rules
of subsections (a) and (b) to a qualified State declared
disaster in the same manner as a disaster, fire, or action
otherwise described in subsection (a)
claims.note: Permissive 'may' (not 'shall') confirms discretion — the IRS is not required to grant.

claims.claim: It covers state-declared disasters but does not otherwise change the rules for federally declared disasters beyond the longer extension period.
claims.sourceSpan: Mandatory Extensions Extended to 120 Days
claims.note: The only cross-cutting change to existing 7508A (which covers federally declared disasters) is the 60->120 day mandatory-extension change in subsection (b); subsection (a) is additive (new state path). No other federal-disaster rule is amended.
